g.text: One query, two clocks — and append-only versus updating
TUMBLE(et) vs TUMBLE(pt) differ on 3 of 4 windows · 4 rows never revised, 2 window revised
2 // Two of a row's five columns are CLOCKS, which ch01 established:
3 // et = event time, when it happened · pt = processing time, when we saw it
4 // v = the value being aggregated · key = the GROUP BY column
5 type Row { id, key, et, pt, v }
6 // primitive: EVENTS — the book's 9 rows, in ARRIVAL order (tools/stream_seed.js).
7 // EVENTS[7] = (id 7, key "b", et 50, pt 280, v 4) <- the late one
8 // primitive: NONE — no value. Distinct from a value of 0.
9 // primitive: WIN — the TUMBLE size, in seconds. WIN = 120
10 // primitive: PERIOD — the HOP slide, in seconds. PERIOD = 60
11 // primitive: GAP — the SESSION gap, in seconds. GAP = 120
12 // primitive: LAG — the watermark's assumed worst-case skew. LAG = 60
13 // primitive: KEYS — the distinct GROUP BY values. KEYS = ["a", "b"]
14 // primitive: append(xs, x) — xs with x added at the end. append([1], 2) = [1,2]
15 // primitive: sum(ids) — total v over those row ids.
17 // primitive: watermarkAfter(i) — highest et through i, minus LAG.
22 // primitive: FILTER_V — the WHERE threshold. FILTER_V = 5
23 // primitive: bucketOf(row, clock) — the TUMBLE bucket, read off ONE column.
26 // function: runFilter() — SELECT * FROM clicks WHERE v > FILTER_V.
27 // Every output row is a FACT: it matched, and nothing later unmatches it.
37 // function: runTumble(clock) — SELECT SUM(v) ... GROUP BY TUMBLE(<clock>, WIN).
38 // The clock is a PARAMETER: there is no second code path for processing time.
51 // function: disagree(a, b) — the buckets where the two clocks differ.
61 // function: sinkNeeds(r) — what a sink must support for that result stream.
68 // function: main() — THE CALLER: two queries, two clocks, two sink contracts.
Step 1/0 — a filter produces facts, which nothing can revise
`e.v > FILTER_V` is decided from the row alone — no later row can change whether id 2 matched. That is why the mode is APPEND-ONLY, and it is readable from
the query shape rather than measured: a `WHERE` has no state to revise.

Step 2/0 — the clock is a PARAMETER, not a second code path
For id 7, `b` is 240 with `clock` = "pt" and 0 with "et" — 2 windows apart. One argument, and the row lands somewhere else entirely. In SQL that argument
is three characters of the query text.

Step 3/0 — so 3 of the 4 buckets hold different sums
Read the two heap rows against each other at bucket 0: 19 and 15. Both Results came from the same function over the same rows. Neither is a bug, and
nothing in the engine could prefer one.

Step 4/0 — and the mode decides what the sink must support
`sinkNeeds` reads only `r.mode`, which was set by the query shape — so the sink contract is derivable before the pipeline runs. `facts` needs INSERT;
`byEvent` needs UPSERT, because window [12:00, 12:02) will go from 15 to 19.
